title: Largest Plus Sign
summary: Given an integer n, you have an n x n binary grid where all values are initially 1's except for some specified indices marked as 0.
statement: Given an integer n, you have an n x n binary grid where all values are initially 1's except for some specified indices marked as 0. The task is to find the largest axis-aligned plus sign of 1's in the grid. A plus sign of order k has a center at grid[r][c] == 1 and four arms of length k - 1 extending up, down, left, and right, all filled with 1's. If no such plus sign exists, return 0.
constraints: Begin with an n by n grid of ones and set listed mine coordinates to zero.
A plus order is one plus its equal arm length in four cardinal directions.
Return the greatest order, or zero if every cell is mined.
hints: At each cell the order is the minimum consecutive-one length in four directions.
Compute left/right/up/down run lengths through directional sweeps.
Store running minima and take the maximum after all four directions.
A plus of order k exists exactly when all four directional lengths are at least k.
editorial: A plus of order k exists exactly when all four directional lengths are at least k.

tests.explanation: The largest surviving axis-aligned plus has order two.
The only cell is mined, so no plus exists.
